metadata.clan_summary:
[bold #D75FFF]◆ EPIC sase-1ux[/bold #D75FFF]
[dim]  Title: [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]Make failed agent sessions and clans unmistakable[/bold #D7AFFF]
[dim]   Goal: [#D7D7AF][/dim]When an agent session or clan stops on a failure, every Agents-tab [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]surface says so: the row, the BY_STATUS section, the count chips, [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]the waves and jump strips, and the detail panels all read FAILED [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]and agree with each other. The cause and the next step are one [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]glance away. A staged handoff the host refused to adopt shows as [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]NOT ADOPTED, never as a phantom RUNNING with a ticking clock.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim] Counts: [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]5[dim][/bold #D7AFFF] phases[dim][/dim] · [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]5[dim][/bold #D7AFFF] waves[/dim]
[dim]   Path: [#87AFFF][/dim]plan:202611/[bold #87AFFF][/#87AFFF]failed_clan_visibility.md[/bold #87AFFF]
[dim] Prompt: [#87AFFF][/dim]prompts/202611/failed_clan_visibility.md[/#87AFFF]
[dim]   Bead: [#87AFFF][/dim]sase-1ux[/#87AFFF]
[dim]   Page: [#87AFFF][/dim]https://github.com/sase-org/sase--beads/blob/main/pages/sase-1ux/[bold #87AFFF][/#87AFFF]README.md[/bold #87AFFF]
[dim]  1 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Project held staged monitors as a first-class state in [/bold #D7AFFF]       [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
      [bold #D7AFFF]sase-core[/bold #D7AFFF]
    [#AF87FF]core-held[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]core-held: in sase-core, project a staged monitor member whose [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]`monitor_stage_held` flag is set as monitor turn state `held`. Add `NOT [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]ADOPTED` to the status-bucket table as Failed, teach the [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]staged-membership facts about `held`, expose a binding for Python [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]fallback loaders, and make previously indexed held members re-project.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  2 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Consume the held state in sase and keep the held flag truthful[bold black on #FFD75F][/bold #D7AFFF] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]held-state[dim] · [dim][/dim]after core-held[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]held-state: bucket `held` as Failed but nonterminal and never in flight.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]Show the member as `NOT ADOPTED ‖` with no ticking clock, move it to the[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]settled monitor lane, and route the filesystem fallback loaders through [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]the binding. Make every not-adopted path set the durable held flag and [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]every successful readopt clear it.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  3 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]One failure-aware session rollup that every surface consumes[/bold #D7AFFF]  [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]session-rollup[dim] · [dim][/dim]after held-state[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]session-rollup: not-adopted members never count as started work. A [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]failed turn stays the session's state until a real later turn supersedes[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]it, for both plan and plain roots. Clan roster, waves, tribe summary, [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]BY_STATUS, and count chips all read the one session rollup. A [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]`FailureFocus` record carries the cause to presentation, and a [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]cross-surface consistency test pins it all.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  4 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Failure signals on Agents-tab rows, waves, and jump strips[/bold #D7AFFF]    [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]row-signals[dim] · [dim][/dim]after session-rollup[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]row-signals: render the failure clearly in the list. Add a clan-row [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]cause chip naming the failed member and its cause, show the failure time[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]instead of a running hourglass on Failed rollups, and draw a red ✗ wave [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]pip and ▶→✗ in WAVES. Put the ‖ glyph in SESSION TURNS and add a visual [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]golden for the incident shape.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  5 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]NEEDS ATTENTION callout in session and clan detail panels, [/bold #D7AFFF]   [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
      [bold #D7AFFF]plus docs[/bold #D7AFFF]
    [#AF87FF]attention-callout[dim] · [dim][/dim]after row-signals[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]attention-callout: a left-barred NEEDS ATTENTION callout at the top of [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]the session and clan detail panels. It says which turn failed, the [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]cause, any not-adopted handoff, the downstream members it blocks, and [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]the exact next step. The tribe NEEDS ATTENTION entry reuses it. Update [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]the status, glyph, and monitor docs, and add panel goldens.[/#D7D7AF]
